at: Kim Yongsu walks that trench
alt: Yongsu walks a trench of sitting men, helmet under his arm
scene: EXPOSITION of the losing fight, before anyone is saved. Low along a muddy trench: young Kim Yongsu, twenty-four, helmet tucked under one arm, mid-stride, mouth open still talking, one hand hauling a sitting spearman up by the collar. Behind him a row of Silla men sit in the mud and will not stand. Across the trench, up on a pit, one Goguryeo captain stands with hands on his hips, laughing. Torn red Goguryeo banners with a black three-legged crow in a studded sun-ring. Silla blue cloth on Yongsu only. Storm-lit afternoon, one hard shaft through dust.

at: the company that was meant to take the pits
alt: The field at Nangbi: pits, a sitting trench, Goguryeo already out of the fort
scene: WIDE SCENE-SETTING of the battle, tiny figures, before the white horse. A hill fort with its gate open. In front of it a line of pits, and Goguryeo men already formed beyond them under red banners with a black three-legged crow in a studded sun-ring. In the foreground a Silla trench full of men sitting down, blue cloth, spears planted and abandoned. One Goguryeo captain stands on a pit like it is a stage. Autumn field, long raking light, dust, no hero in the center.

at: Yushin comes through on the white horse
alt: Yushin rides into Surabol under pine branches, the Goguryeo flag across his saddle
scene: THE RETURN. The west gate of Surabol, giwa roofs, pine branches tied over the lintel, a crowd in simple white. Kim Yushin rides through on a white horse, a torn red Goguryeo flag with its black three-legged crow unfurled across the saddle, not folded. Three horses behind him, Kim Yongsu, younger, talking sideways to the rider beside him while his eyes stay on the flag. Cold clear light, one shaft on the red silk.

at: lays the flag on the steps
alt: Yushin lays the Goguryeo flag on the palace steps before King Jinpyung
scene: The palace steps. Kim Yushin has just dismounted and is laying the torn red Goguryeo flag flat on the stone, both hands, head bowed. King Jinpyung stands two steps up in a thin coat, looking at the flag, not at the crowd. Behind Yushin, his father Seohyun stands, not kneeling, one hand half-raised as if to fix a helmet that is already straight. Pine branches shake at the edge of frame. Crowd bokeh below.

at: walks them down the long hall
alt: Before dawn King Guhae carries his smallest son down the painted hall
scene: EXPOSITION, the promise. A long Gaya hall before dawn, one oil lamp on the floor, a painted wall of clouds just catching the first light. King Guhae in a sleeping robe walks the hall carrying his smallest son on one hip. The boy, Muryuk, points at the painting. Two older brothers trail behind in sleeping clothes, barefoot, complaining. Worm's-eye from the floor beside the lamp. The boy's cone helm is not on yet.

at: sets it on the boy’s head
alt: Guhae sets the tall Gaya cone on his son's head and it covers his eyes
scene: On a sunlit threshold. King Guhae lowers a tall iron Gaya cone helm onto small Muryuk's head. The helm comes down over the boy's eyes. The boy stands very straight anyway, mouth open, about to say he can't see. Guhae is smiling and already sorry. Low three-quarter. Harbour light through the door, purple #8B5CF6 only as a silk sash catching the sun.

at: The river is full of men
alt: Golden Gaya's harbour on fire, the river full of men, the cone helm still at the ford
scene: WIDE of the fall. A harbour of iron sheds pouring black smoke. The river is full of men who are not swimming. At the ford, small in the lower third, one tall Gaya cone helm still fighting, Muryuk, his father's guard behind him. Silla spears pouring down the far bank, far more of them. Morning, one hard shaft through the smoke.

at: He comes in behind a pine
alt: Muryuk behind a pine, listening, sword lowered
scene: He has just arrived. Muryuk, seventeen, clean-shaven, pressed to the dark side of a pine, one eye past the bark. Sword lowered, not raised. Beyond the tree, out of focus, a canopy, two seated shapes, no detail. His mouth is shut. Dappled noon, the tree a hard black vertical splitting the frame.

at: His back finds the pine
alt: Muryuk's back against the pine, helm strap wet, eyes gone
scene: The same pine, later by a minute. Muryuk's BACK is flat against the bark, head tipped to the wood, eyes wet and open, not looking at the canopy anymore. The tall cone helm is still on, the strap dark and wet under his chin. Sword point-down in a loose hand. He makes no sound. One shaft through needles, the rest of the frame in the tree's shadow.

at: If we are to surrender, I have one condition
alt: Guhae on his knees under the canopy, bargaining with the king of Silla
scene: THE CONVERSATION under the pines. A cloth canopy. The king of Silla, Beopheung, sits on a camp stool, patient, one hand open. King Guhae of Gaya is on his knees in front of him, not in chains, talking, one palm up, begging without shame and not looking away. A writing table between them with a blank sheet. Noon shade, dust in one shaft. No third person in frame.

at: lays his sword on the ground
alt: Muryuk kneels beside his father and lays his sword down before the king of Silla
scene: The clearing, from the other side. Muryuk walks in as if he has only just arrived and is kneeling beside his father, laying his straight ring-pommel sword on the grass before the seated Silla king. Guhae, still on his knees, has just said his son's name. Muryuk's face is closed. The pine he was hiding behind is behind him, empty.

at: Suulbu walked this city with a list
alt: Suulbu walks Surabol at night with a list and a lamp
scene: VILLAIN. Prince Suulbu, not yet old, walks a dark Surabol lane alone with a lamp in one hand and a long unfolded list in the other, reading it as he walks. His face is bored and contemptuous, as if the names were furniture. Behind him, at a distance, two men wait at a shut gate. One hard lamp-light up into his face. No blood. The list has no readable writing, only rows of dark strokes.

at: I struck off a hundred of Jinji’s men
alt: Suulbu at a table built for twelve, striking names off a roll
scene: A long table built for twelve, three places set. Suulbu sits at the head and strikes through a name on a roll with a wet brush, not looking up, mouth mid-sentence, pleased with the arithmetic. The other chairs are empty. One lamp. The brush flicks. The paper shows only black strokes, no readable letters.

at: Every house in Sabi agrees
alt: Deer Rock above Sabi at dusk, the sealed box, a man from every house below
scene: EXPOSITION of Deer Rock. Dusk over Sabi: a bare dark rock above the roofs, a small sealed box on its crown, one monk's lamp beside it. At the foot, a ring of tiny anonymous silhouettes, one from each great house, watching each other more than the box. River mist starting. One gold lamp. No faces.

at: King Mu seals the box
alt: King Mu seals the box with his own hand as the sun goes down
scene: Sunset on the rock. King Mu kneels and presses his own seal onto a small box, concentrating, amused. Crown prince Euija stands a step back with a jug he is not supposed to have, watching the seal, not the view. The rock is still wet. Long red light, the box the bright thing.

at: the whole rock is beaded
alt: At dawn the rock sweats, and King Mu climbs it to break his own seal
scene: First light. The whole rock is beaded and running, as if it had rained. King Mu, too old for the climb, is halfway up, one hand on the wet stone, going to break his own seal. Mist in the river below. The box glints at the top. High-key pale sky, the wet rock the dark thing.

at: the Eastern Commander goes to the High Summit
alt: Yeon's little column: six riders, one cart, an ox, the long road south
scene: EXPOSITION of the journey. A wide thaw road. A covered ox-cart, six riders, one spare horse. Yeon Gesomun rides a red bay beside the cart, annoyed, gloves on. His wife lifts the cart flap, one hand out, telling him something about the ruts. A young soldier walks at the wheel. Fortress small behind them. Pale spring sky, mud, one shaft.

at: lying flat on the ice
alt: The soldier called Eye lies on the river ice, listening
scene: A river frozen white from bank to bank. A young soldier lies flat on the ice with one ear pressed to it, eyes wide, one eye looking slightly aside. Yeon stands over him in his commander's coat, skeptical, about to order the cart across. The ox and cart wait on the bank, small. Cold high-key light, the ice a white plane, the two men the dark ink.

at: the ice opens like a mouth
alt: The ice opens and Yeon goes in after the horse
scene: The ice has opened like a mouth. A spare horse is in to the neck. Yeon Gesomun is in the water to the chest, boots and coat, reaching for the bridle, furious. On the far bank, already across, the ox-cart and his wife watching. Splintered white plates, black water, one cold shaft.

at: On the yard rail sit three men
alt: Three old classmates on the frozen Hwarang rail, boys drilling below
scene: EXPOSITION. Midwinter. The Hwarang yard below the Moon Palace, frozen hard. Three men sit on the rail: Yushin looking up the hill, Bidam with beads, Alchun broad and easy. Below them, small, a class of boys drills on the ice and keeps glancing up. Pale high-key winter sky, breath, one low sun.

at: Smoke where there should be no smoke
alt: Night fog at the valley mouth, cookfire smoke where no one should be camped
scene: SCENE-SETTING of the valley at night. Fog in the mouth of a narrow valley. Bidam, on foot, one hand raised to stop the boys behind him. Alchun beside him, already looking at the smoke. Down in the valley, cookfire smoke and a loose camp of five hundred, small, lanterns. No fight yet. One fire as the only warm light.

at: Uso climbs the biggest rock
alt: A Baekje captain alone on the biggest rock, a bow, the valley below him lost
scene: The biggest rock in the valley. A Baekje captain stands on top with a bow, one arrow left, the camp below him already broken and smoking. Alchun climbs the rock with empty hands, looking up, a hole in his sleeve. Worm's-eye from the stone. Torch bokeh far below. One shaft on the bow.

at: sets a third cup
alt: Namgun and Namsan at their father's table, a third cup poured for no one
scene: Their father's hall at night, too big. Namgun and Namsan sit at the low table. Namsan has just set down a third cup and is not pouring it. Namgun stares at the cup. Empty chair between them, their father's. One lamp. Neither is touching the cup.

at: The ring is warm
alt: Namseng kneels in the mud outside a shut gate, a child's gold ring in his hand
scene: Outside a shut fortress gate. Namseng is off his horse, kneeling in the mud, a child's gold ring in a hand that will not close. His face is empty. Up on the wall, small, his brother Namgun looks down and has just thrown it. A boy of fifteen stands by the horse, looking at the horse, not at his father. Overcast, the ring the one bright thing.

at: looking for a window
alt: Namseng in a Western coat looks for a shuttered window, not at the wall
scene: Namseng at the head of a column in a Tang officer's coat, vermilion cloth, steel helm, reining in. He is not looking at the city wall. He is looking at one shuttered window in a big house under the hill. The shutter is closed. His face wants it to open. Dust, banners tiny behind him, the window the subject.

at: Namsan opens the banner himself
alt: Namsan unfurls the white banner at the gate and looks back for a brother who is not there
scene: The south-west gate, from inside. Namsan unfurls a plain white banner himself, both hands, and looks back up the wall. The wall has a sentry, not his brother. Behind him a frightened king and a small knot of officials in white. Morning, the white silk the brightest thing, the city already dim.

at: watches the towers take light
alt: Namseng sits his horse on the north road and watches the gate towers catch fire
scene: Night on the north road. Namseng sits a horse in the Western coat and does not ride in. Ahead, the gate towers of Pyongyang catch fire one after another, like lamps being lit. His mouth is just open on a name. He is small against the burning city. One fire as the key, his face lit from it.

at: Look at me. All three.
alt: Gesomun, dying, makes his three sons look at him at once
scene: A small too-warm room. Yeon Gesomun sits up in a great chair, weaker than the chair, and points at his three sons: look at me. Namseng stands formal and still. Namgun is crying and angry about it. Namsan stares at the floorboards. For this one breath all three faces are turned to their father. One lamp on the floor. Gulgul is a shoulder in the dark foreground, out of focus.
